Accumulated local effects of one input

Source: R/xpl.R
xpale.Rd

The effect of one input on a prediction, measured only where the data are (Apley and Zhu 2020): the range of the column is cut at its quantiles into intervals, each row's prediction is taken at the upper and at the lower edge of its own interval with its other inputs as they are, the differences are averaged within each interval and accumulated from the lowest edge. Unlike partial dependence (xppdp()) no row is moved far from where it lies, so an input correlated with others (prior arrests and age, say) is not credited with their effects.

Usage

xpale(x, f, v, y = NULL, nbin = 10, lctl = list())

# S3 method for class 'xpale'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

The rows at which to predict: a numeric matrix, its column names those f sees, no missing values.

f

The prediction function: a function of a numeric matrix returning one finite number per row, or the names of learners of suplrn() ("glm", "lasso", "ridge", "enet", "forest").

v

The input: the name or the number of one column of x.

y

The outcome at the rows of x, needed only to fit the learners named in f.

nbin

The intervals asked for: one whole number from 1 to 67108864.

lctl

The settings of the learners named in f: a list named by arguments of suplrn() (fam, nfold, fold, disc, alpha, nlam, nfin, ntree, mtry, seed); empty for a function.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class xpale, a list: ale, a data frame with the edges (z) and the centred accumulated effect there (ale); bins, a data frame with one row per interval (lo, hi its edges, n its rows, eff the mean difference of the predictions across it); and term.

Details

The edges are the column's minimum and its quantiles at 1/nbin, 2/nbin, ..., 1 (quantile() type 1), repeated values dropped, so there are at most nbin intervals; each interval holds the rows above its lower edge up to its upper one, the first its lower edge too. The effects are centred so that their mean over the rows, the effect taken as linear within each interval, is 0: the centring of the authors' 'ALEPlot'. The rows are written and the effects accumulated in the compiled core; f is called once on all the rows.

References

Apley, D. W. and Zhu, J. (2020). Visualizing the effects of predictor variables in black box supervised learning models. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B, 82(4), 1059-1086. doi:10.1111/rssb.12377

Examples

set.seed(4)
age <- runif(200, 18, 60)
prior <- rpois(200, (60 - age) / 10)
x <- cbind(prior, age)
f <- function(m) plogis(-1 + 0.5 * m[, "prior"] - 0.03 * m[, "age"])
xpale(x, f, "age", nbin = 5)
#> xpale: accumulated local effects of age over 5 interval(s)
#>         z         ale
#>  18.12276  0.11761138
#>  26.93682  0.06485629
#>  35.43904  0.01050556
#>  43.48715 -0.03293827
#>  52.64466 -0.06308333
#>  59.85774 -0.07813159
